claims.text: The Flickr30K dataset is a collection of over 30,000 images with 5 crowdsourced descriptions each.
claims.quote: The Flickr30K dataset BIBREF0 is a collection of over 30,000 images with 5 crowdsourced descriptions each.

claims.text: The dataset contains linguistic bias and unwarranted inferences.
claims.quote: I have divided these descriptions into two classes: linguistic bias and unwarranted inferences.

claims.text: Linguistic bias corresponds to annotators' word choices when confronted with an image that may or may not match their stereotypical expectancies.
claims.quote: The former corresponds to the annotators' choice of words when confronted with an image that may or may not match their stereotypical expectancies.

claims.text: Unwarranted inferences correspond to annotators going beyond what the physical data can tell us and expanding descriptions based on past experiences and knowledge of the world.
claims.quote: The latter corresponds to the tendency of annotators to go beyond what the physical data can tell us, and expand their descriptions based on their past experiences and knowledge of the world.

claims.text: Negations overtly display the annotator's prior beliefs.
claims.quote: Negations are much more overtly displaying the annotator's prior beliefs.

claims.text: The model achieves improved performance on PDTB for both implicit and explicit discourse relation classification.
claims.quote: achieves improved performance on PDTB for both implicit discourse relation classification and explicit discourse relation classification

claims.text: The work focuses on the top-level discourse relation senses consisting of four major semantic classes: Comparison, Contingency, Expansion and Temporal.
claims.quote: we focus on the top-level discourse relation senses which are consist of four major semantic classes: Comparison (Comp), Contingency (Cont), Expansion (Exp) and Temporal (Temp)

claims.text: The proposed models are mainly evaluated using the four-way multi-class classification setting.
claims.quote: we mainly evaluate our proposed models using the four-way multi-class classification setting

claims.text: The full ensemble model improves macro F1-score by 3.02 for implicit relations and 0.96 for explicit relations.
claims.quote: The full model achieves performance boosting of (51.84 - 48.82 = 3.02) and (94.17 - 93.21 = 0.96) in macro F1-scores for predicting implicit and explicit discourse relations respectively.

claims.text: The paragraph-level model improved the macro-average F1-score by over 7 percent compared with the baseline Bi-LSTM model.
claims.quote: this model has greatly improved implicit relation classification performance across all the four relations and improved the macro-average F1-score by over 7 percents

claims.text: Compared with the baseline Bi-LSTM model with tensor, the model improved the macro-average F1-score by 2.2 percent.
claims.quote: overall improved the macro-average F1-score by 2.2 percents

claims.text: A question generation model is used to generate a question based on the semantics of a candidate answer.
claims.quote: we present the generation model which generates a question based on the semantics of a candidate answer

claims.text: The question generation model provides each candidate answer with a score by measuring semantic relevance between the question and the generated question.
claims.quote: The question generation model provides each candidate answer with a score by measuring semantic relevance between the question and the generated question based on the semantics of the candidate answer.

claims.text: The question generation model takes the path between an anchor and the candidate answer and outputs a question.
claims.quote: Our question generation model takes the path between an “anchor” and the candidate answer, and outputs a question.

claims.text: The generation-based model takes semantics of a candidate answer as input and generates a question.
claims.quote: It takes semantics of a candidate answer as the input and generates a question

claims.text: The baseline models are QA PGNet and Multi-decoder QA PGNet with lookup table embedding.
claims.quote: We consider QA PGNet and Multi-decoder QA PGNet with lookup table embedding as baseline models

claims.text: For Dosage extraction, the naive baseline is 'Nearest Number', taking the number nearest to the Medication Name as the prediction.
claims.quote: For Dosage extraction, the baseline we consider is `Nearest Number', where we take the number nearest to the Medication Name as the prediction

claims.text: For Frequency extraction, the naive baseline is 'Random Top-3', predicting a random Frequency tag from the top-3 most frequent ones.
claims.quote: For Frequency extraction, the baseline we consider is `Random Top-3' where we predict a random Frequency tag, from top-3 most frequent ones from our dataset

claims.text: The Transformer layer works better than the RNN layer on top of BERT, as ToBERT outperforms RoBERT on Fisher and 20newsgroups by 13.63% and 0.81% respectively.
claims.quote: ToBERT outperforms RoBERT on Fisher and 20newsgroups dataset by 13.63% and 0.81% respectively.

claims.text: ToBERT exploited the pre-trained BERT features better than RoBERT and converged faster.
claims.quote: We also notice that ToBERT model exploited the pre-trained BERT features better than RoBERT. It also converged faster than RoBERT.

claims.text: On CSAT, ToBERT performs slightly worse than RoBERT but it is not statistically significant.
claims.quote: On CSAT, ToBERT performs slightly worse than RoBERT but it is not statistically significant as this dataset is small.

claims.text: The data was collected using the crowdsourcing platform CrowdFlower (CF).
claims.quote: Therefore, we used the crowdsourcing platform CrowdFlower (CF) for our data collection.

claims.text: CF workers used a chat-like interface to help the system with a randomly selected question from training examples of the Simple questions dataset.
claims.quote: A CF worker gets a task instructing them to use our chat-like interface to help the system with a question which is randomly selected from training examples of Simple questions BIBREF7 dataset.

claims.text: Only CF workers from English speaking countries were involved to avoid poor English level of dialogs.
claims.quote: To avoid poor English level of dialogs we involved CF workers from English speaking countries only.

claims.text: The collected dialogs were afterwards annotated by expert annotators.
claims.quote: The collected dialogs has been annotated (see Section "Acknowledgments" ) by expert annotators afterwards.

claims.text: The dataset was collected with 1900 dialogs and 8533 turns.
claims.quote: We collected the dataset with 1900 dialogs and 8533 turns.
